result:
If I could change one thing about the world, I think I'd want people to have an easier time really hearing each other—not just listening to respond, but actually taking in what someone else means and why it matters to them, even across deep disagreements.

So much conflict, cruelty, and even ordinary unhappiness seems to come from people talking past each other, assuming the worst about motives, or just not having the bandwidth to imagine a different vantage point. If that one capacity were stronger across the board, a lot of other good things might follow—better politics, more durable relationships, more creative problem-solving on hard collective issues like climate change or inequality. Not because people would suddenly agree on everything, but because they'd disagree with more accuracy and less contempt.

I'll admit this is a bit of a cop-out answer compared to, say, "eliminate disease" or "end poverty"—those are huge and concrete. But I keep coming back to communication and understanding because they seem upstream of so many other problems. A world that was better at this might be slower to fix some things and faster to fix others, but it'd probably be a less cruel place to disagree in.

What's your answer? I'm curious whether you'd go for something more structural—like fixing a resource or institutional problem—or something more like what I picked.
